correctness.rationale: For unweighted n-site path with all intervals and nonnegative f,g, max of interval averages preserves perturbation range [min(g−f),max(g−f)] pointwise, yielding L_n≤n−1. For q=floor(n/24), m=12q, f is 1 on first m sites, then alternates 3/4 and zero for m sites, with g=f+ε1_[1,m], ε=1/(100m), and zero padding. Odd tail indices d∈[8q+3,12q] have both maximal values 3/4; prefix averages even after perturbation are below this. Every tested even index has a maximizing interval touching the unit block and gains at least ε/2, since local tail intervals attain at most 1/2. At 4q−3 intervening edges D=M(g)−M(f) oscillates between zero and ≥ε/2, giving L_n≥2q−3/2. On the integer line the same witness has input BV variation 2ε, and homogeneity rescales arbitrary input pairs to zero while retaining divergent ratios. Independently enumerated exact Fraction interval maxima for q=1,2,3, verifying the odd/even response and lower bounds; universal proof is the prefix comparison not q≤3 tests.
residual_risks: Only uniform counting measure and all contiguous intervals; conventional absolute-value maximal operator agrees only because witnesses are nonnegative.
The BV norm on infinite line includes a second perturbation jump; explicit factor 2 was accounted for.
